answer: Decaying activity grove. Each identity accrues a visible thread of on-chain actions; influence weight decays with idle time, so dormant sybils fade. To reactivate, an identity must re-earn weight by paying a rising cost per action tied to grove crowding. A zephyr of fresh identities can't flood the grove because each one's reactivation cost scales with total recent identity churn. Attacker pays per-identity reactivation plus churn premium; cost rises superlinearly with clone count, making mass sybil activation uneconomical.
